Diagnose time series, optionally within dplyr groups

Source: R/diagnose_timeseries.R
diagnose_timeseries.Rd

Computes descriptive statistics, checks the time grid, and screens for unusual observations after removing trend and (when specified) seasonality. Regular, complete series also receive autocorrelation diagnostics and, when feasts and urca are installed, KPSS and Phillips-Perron tests.

Usage

diagnose_timeseries(
  data,
  x,
  y,
  .period = NULL,
  .breaks = c("none", "level", "trend"),
  .features = c("summary", "outliers", "seasonality", "stationarity", "autocorrelation")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, optionally grouped with dplyr::group_by(). Each group must contain one time series.

x

Time column. (Unquoted.)

y

Numeric measurement column. (Unquoted.)

.period

Seasonal period in observations, e.g. 12 for monthly data with annual seasonality. NULL infers annual seasonality for aligned calendar months/quarters; other indices default to 1 (no seasonality). This sets seasonality, not the spacing of the time index.

.breaks

One of "none" (default), "level", or "trend". The latter two require strucchange and fit up to three breaks with BIC selection on seasonally adjusted data. Break searches are limited to 30–2000 observations and segments of at least 15% of the series (and at least 10 observations) to bound computational cost.

.features

Diagnostics to compute: any of "summary", "outliers", "seasonality", "stationarity", and "autocorrelation". Defaults to all of these. Structural breaks are independently enabled by .breaks.

Value

A tibble with one row per group (one row for ungrouped input). Scalar columns describe the series. List columns contain tests, outliers, breakpoints, correlation, decomposition, and notes. Break dates denote the first observation in the new segment; their confidence limits use the same convention. Unavailable diagnostics are empty tables with an explanation in notes. n_breaks is NA when break detection is unavailable or not requested, and zero when the fitted model selects no break dates.

Details

Missing/non-finite observations, duplicate times and irregular or gapped indices are reported without deleting or interpolating observations. They prevent time-dependent diagnostics. Grid inference cannot identify periods absent throughout the data; inspect the inferred interval.

Outliers are candidates with an absolute robust residual score above 4.5, using robust STL for seasonal series and a running median otherwise. A zero MAD uses a numerical tolerance and is reported in notes. At least eight observations are required for residual screening, and seasonal decomposition needs more than two complete seasons. Unit root tests require at least 20 nonconstant observations and run on observed values: KPSS has level stationarity as its null; Phillips-Perron has a unit root as its null. Failure to reject is not proof of either null. These are exploratory diagnostics, not automatic data corrections.

Examples

d <- data.frame(year = 2001:2040, value = sin(1:40) + (1:40) / 10)
diagnose_timeseries(d, year, value)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 32
#>       n n_finite missing non_finite missing_time duplicate_times start end  
#>   <int>    <int>   <int>      <int>        <int>           <int> <chr> <chr>
#> 1    40       40       0          0            0               0 2001  2040 
#> # ℹ 24 more variables: interval <chr>, regular <lgl>, missing_periods <dbl>,
#> #   period <int>, mean <dbl>, median <dbl>, sd <dbl>, min <dbl>, q25 <dbl>,
#> #   q75 <dbl>, max <dbl>, last <dbl>, change <dbl>, change_pct <dbl>,
#> #   trend_strength <dbl>, seasonal_strength <dbl>, n_outliers <int>,
#> #   n_breaks <int>, tests <list>, outliers <list>, breakpoints <list>,
#> #   correlation <list>, decomposition <list>, notes <list>
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data |>
  dplyr::group_by(country, variable) |>
  diagnose_timeseries(date, value, .period = 12)
} # }
